title: A♭ major across the strings · C Standard
summary: Play one octave from A♭2 to A♭3 and return to A♭2.
goal: Play A♭–B♭–C–D♭–E♭–F–G–A♭ with the written open-position fingering, then descend.
body:
This lesson belongs to the C Standard course. For prerequisites, choose lessons marked C Standard.

Before starting: complete First frets and Steady pulse. Tune to C Standard, A4 = 440 Hz.

A♭ major uses A♭, B♭, C, D♭, E♭, F, G. From one A♭ to the next, its steps are tone, tone, semitone, tone, tone, tone, semitone. C–D♭ and G–A♭ are the semitone pairs. This exercise covers A♭2 to A♭3, so the two A♭s are one octave apart.

The fingering stays near frets 0–3. Suggested fingers: index for fret 1, middle for fret 2, ring for fret 3; 0 is open. Follow the written string as well as the fret number. The same pitch can exist elsewhere, but the fretboard is showing the intended path. Audio cannot prove which string you used.

Start at 60 BPM, one quarter note per click. Learn the first two bars ascending, then bars 3–4 descending. The top A♭3 is played once before descending to G3. After a comfortable full repeat, 70 BPM is a useful next tempo. Use the result to choose a smaller fragment when a transition needs more time.

root-c.title: 1. Find the root A♭2
root-c.body: String 5, fret 3 gives A♭2. This is the first and last sounding note of the exercise.

lower-half.title: 2. Play A♭2, B♭2, C3, D♭3
lower-half.body: Bar 1: string 5 fret 3; string 4 frets 0, 2, 3. Count one note on each beat.

upper-half.title: 3. Play E♭3, F3, G3, A♭3
upper-half.body: Bar 2: string 3 frets 0, 2; string 2 frets 0, 1. The last note is A♭3.

descending.title: 4. Descend to A♭2
descending.body: Bars 3–4: G3, F3, E♭3, D♭3, C3, B♭2, A♭2. Reverse the same positions; let only the current note sound.

finish.title: 5. Finish with a rest
finish.body: The final beat of bar 4 is a rest. Stop the last A♭2 and keep counting. Prepare a new practice attempt to repeat the same four bars.
